newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher before All Saints.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher before All Saints.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Thursday before the All Saints holiday with only the expiry of the October options contract in the late afternoon giving a sparkle to otherwise listless trading.

The market did not react to a record September unemployment rate of 12.6 percent and shrugged off a five basis point rate cut by the Bank of France. It took hardly notice of September U.S. jobless claims and consumer spending. But after Wall Street opened and towards the 1500 GMT expiry things livened up.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 15.75 points or 0.74 percent at 2,140.51. Volume was 7.25 billion francs.
Of the volume, six billion francs was related to so-called basket deals prompted by the expiry of the October future contract.
The October future closed at 2,142 on Thursday, against a Wednesday settlement at 2,128.50.
Despite the higher close on Thursday, the blue-chip index was down 1.01 percent on the week due to profit-taking after hitting a two-and-a-half year high last week.
The franc was supported by a European Commission decision to allow France to use a special France Telecom payment towards cutting the budget deficit and single currency qualification.
Lagardere posted a 3.8 percent gain as Thomson bid worries subside and Euro Disney fell 4.74 percent ahead of its financial year results on November 14.
